svg.text: Input metadata of one prefill step
Two prompt chunks packed into one list of 260 rows · values follow the real C++ rules · sequences are illustrative
A: q 60, k 260, blocks [7,2,9], slot 2 B: q 200, k 200, blocks [3,4,5,6], slot 1 ring 134
How are the two chunks packed?
The rows follow each other with no gaps. Offset arrays mark where each chunk starts.
B: rows 60-259 (first chunk of a 400-token prompt, cut at 200)
Where do the new cache entries go?
One slot per new entry. The value -1 means: do not write.
slot_mapping_store_swa [260] state_id * 134 + position % 134, only for the last 134 rows of a chunk
B rows 60-125 (positions 0-65) are older than the ring keeps. Position 134 wraps to ring row 0.
slot_mapping_store_ca["2"] [130] one entry per 2 tokens: block_table[j / 64] * 64 + j % 64
What does each row read from the sliding window?
A gather builds one buffer: 128 history rows per chunk, then all new rows. Pivots describe each row's window.
new rows of this step (A 256-315, B 316-515)
load_segments_swa [3, 4] rows: [src slot, src_begin, src_end, dst_offset]
kv_swa_full_index_pivots [260, 4] [history start, history count, new start, new count]
Simplified: only ratio 2 is shown. The dicts have one entry per compress ratio of the model (C1 and/or C2).
Not shown: input_ids, ks/ke, kv_ca_index_offset_len, load_segments_ca, cu_compressed_seqlens_q (see the deep dive).
